units.en: ⟦0⟧ unlocks different models of armored vehicles, including tanks and armor variants like self-propelled anti-air, self-propelled artillery, and tank destroyers. Thanks to their high breakthrough, tanks can act as armed and armored offensive specialists, while armor variants can act as more heavily armed and armored versions of motorized combat support units. These vehicles are also split into light, medium, heavy, super-heavy versions, and amphibious versions). Light tanks and their variants tend to be fast, inexpensive, but weak, medium tanks and their variants tend to be the most cost-effective but still slower and more expensive than light tanks, and heavy tanks and their variants tend to be the most combat-capable but also by far the most expensive and the ones with the most difficulty with adverse terrain. Super-heavy tanks and their variants are even slower, even more expensive, and even worse in adverse terrain than heavy tanks and can only be used in smaller numbers as ⟦1⟧, but when they can be effectively fielded, they can be incredibly powerful.

With the introduction of special projects in ⟦0⟧ and the accompanying ⟦1⟧, all armor technologies now also generate land warfare breakthrough progress while being researched. Armor technologies are also particularly intertwined with the ⟦2⟧ land warfare special project.

These technologies unlock and improve equipment used by ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧ frontline battalions, as well as for ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, and, with ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧. They can also unlock and improve equipment used by ⟦9⟧ battalions.

Great War TankTanks in World War I were developed separately and simultaneously by the United Kingdom and France as a means to break the deadlock of trench warfare on the Western Front. The name Tank was adopted by the British during the early stages of their development, as a security measure to conceal their purpose. Early tanks were armed with machine guns and small cannons, moved slowly, and were armored only enough to stop small arms fire.

These technologies unlock and improve equipment used by ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ and, with ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧. They can help unlock medium tanks technologies as well. They are also required to eventually unlock amphibious tanks.

All tank models (except for amphibious ones) have three armor variants that can be unlocked through individual technologies: ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and ⟦2⟧. The buttons for each of these can be found next to their corresponding tank model technology.

Switching production from the base model to a variant results in a much lower loss of production efficiency than usual; it can be useful to co-opt an obsolete tank line into producing variants rather than upgraded tanks. This represents the historical practice of repurposing obsolete tanks into specialized variants, which was much cheaper and quicker than simply scrapping them. Light, medium, heavy, super-heavy and modern variants each have their own battalion types and will not request equipment from other lines. Some variants also use less equipment than their corresponding tank battalions.

⟦0⟧, also known as TDs, are dedicated, armored anti-tank vehicles. They are essentially an anti-tank gun on a tank chassis. Tank destroyer battalions can be thought of as the armored equivalent of ⟦1⟧ battalions. Historically, most tank destroyers had a casemate with a narrow range of travel for the gun instead of a turret, and many early models were open-topped.

Tank destroyers generally trade higher piercing and hard attack for lower soft attack, lower organization, and far lower breakthrough. Since ⟦0⟧ of a division's piercing and ⟦1⟧ of its armor comes from the battalions in the division with the highest values for those, even just a single tank destroyer battalion can significantly boost the combat-effectiveness of an entire division and reduce its need for unarmored anti-tank battalions or ⟦2⟧.

Light Tank Destroyer ITank Destroyers are tanks with a larger than normal gun in a fixed mounting in place of a turret. Light Tank Destroyers are based on the chassis of Light Tanks, which means they are fairly mobile but do not carry particularly powerful guns compared to heavier TDs.

Light Tank Destroyer IITank Destroyers are tanks with a larger than normal gun in a fixed mounting in place of a turret. Light Tank Destroyers are based on the chassis of Light Tanks, which means they are fairly mobile but do not carry particularly powerful guns compared to heavier TDs.

Light Tank Destroyer IIITank Destroyers are tanks with a larger than normal gun in a fixed mounting in place of a turret. Light Tank Destroyers are based on the chassis of Light Tanks, which means they are fairly mobile but do not carry particularly powerful guns compared to heavier TDs.
These technologies unlock and improve equipment used by ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ battalions.

Medium Tank Destroyer ITank Destroyers are tanks with a larger than normal gun in a fixed mounting in place of a turret. Medium Tank Destroyers are based on the chassis of Medium Tanks, meaning they are fairly mobile and carry respectable firepower.

Medium Tank Destroyer IITank Destroyers are tanks with a larger than normal gun in a fixed mounting in place of a turret. Medium Tank Destroyers are based on the chassis of Medium Tanks, meaning they are fairly mobile and carry respectable firepower.

Medium Tank Destroyer IIITank Destroyers are tanks with a larger than normal gun in a fixed mounting in place of a turret. Medium Tank Destroyers are based on the chassis of Medium Tanks, meaning they are fairly mobile and carry respectable firepower.
Modern Tank DestroyerModern Tank Destroyers are an evolution of earlier light and medium TDs, providing mobility and stealth to heavy armor.
These technologies unlock and improve equipment used by ⟦0⟧ battalions and ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.
Heavy Tank Destroyer IA heavy tank with the turret removed to carry an even larger gun in a fixed mounting.
Heavy Tank Destroyer IIA heavy tank with the turret removed to carry an even larger gun in a fixed mounting.
Super Heavy Tank DestroyerA super heavy tank chassis with more frontal armour and an even larger gun in a fixed mount instead of a turret.
Heavy Tank Destroyer IIIA heavy tank with the turret removed to carry an even larger gun in a fixed mounting.

⟦0⟧, also known as self-propelled guns or SPGs, are essentially artillery guns on tank chassis. They can be thought of as the armored equivalent of ⟦1⟧. Historically, most self-propelled artillery had a fixed gun mounting with limited horizontal travel instead of a turret, and many early models were open-topped.

Self-propelled artillery generally trade higher soft attack for lower hard attack, lower piercing, lower hardness, lower armor, lower organization, and far lower breakthrough. However, they are still more heavily armored than their truck-drawn counterparts. Since ⟦0⟧ of a division's armor comes from the battalion in the division with the highest armor, they can be particularly useful as an armored complement to divisions that otherwise would have used an unarmored artillery piece for its soft attack.
A small artillery cannon mounted on a light chassis, a light SPG does not pack the firepower of its larger brethren, but they are more mobile.

⟦0⟧, also known as SPAA, are dedicated anti-air guns mounted on tank chassis. They can be thought of as the armored equivalent of ⟦1⟧. Historically, dedicated armored vehicles carrying anti-air guns came late in the war, the earliest example being the Hungarian 40M Nimród in 1943. Most anti-air vehicles were mounted on trucks instead, making them more like ⟦2⟧.

Self-propelled anti-air gain air attack at the expense of slightly higher production cost, lower soft attack, lower hard attack, lower piercing, lower hardness, lower armor, lower organization, and far lower breakthrough. While this may seem like a huge sacrifice for something so minor, SPAA are still relatively fast and armored and still have enough piercing to pierce lighter, obsolete armor and ⟦0⟧. Since ⟦1⟧ of a division's armor comes from the battalion in the division with the highest armor, they can be particularly useful as an armored complement to divisions that would want some anti-air capabilities anyway and would otherwise be completely unarmored.
